title: Dodging the draft and the spread of drugs
summary: Hall says musicians took drugs to be rejected by the army and that he never saw heroin used.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Now, we were also talking about, you know, the scene changed there during the war years and because of people not wanting to go into the army, that they got into the drugs then?
Right. To be rejected for the examination. So, everybody was going overboard and taking things that would get them rejected, even to going to faggotry.
Yeah.
That was the last place you would go would be the psychiatrist, right?
Yeah.
And they --
Get a letter or something?
Yeah. He's not fit for army duty or something, then he got wise to this and they sent everybody out to, was it Governor's Island?
Yeah.
For a three-day rest of all your habits.
The benzedrine inhalers --
Yeah, by that time you were straight and they put you in. (Laughter)
So what you are saying is you think that because, the thing about drugs then, it led people to try heroin because it was just a general drug culture started?
Yeah, but I didn't know from heroin.
Yeah.
I never saw heroin. I didn't know anybody that was using it. I mean, I didn't see them use it or anything but the end result was that they were using it.
Because certainly at the time you recorded with Sonny Stitt he was probably into it because that was the --
Well, you see, I didn't know anything,
well, I didn't know the habits of a lot of guys. I didn't know Sonny Stitt was into it at that point. I found out later, maybe.
And of course, he had played on the Billy Eckstine band and that notorious, there were a lot of people, were you know, strung out on that band.
Well, without naming names, I would say that these were the guys that hung out together, you know, whatever their culture was, for satisfying their needs.
